spec_findings: The binding requires that only the owner sets status to approved, but the design gives no point where that rule could be enforced or observed: every role writes the status field directly with fs.writeFile and nothing records who wrote it.
defects: No function or service sits on every status change, so an agent can set approved with a plain file write and nothing refuses or records it; the property is unenforced by design.
not_covered: The property 'an agent cannot perform the owner's transition': it cannot be tested with the current design, because there is no gate to attempt the transition against and no record of the writer to check a refusal or a log against
escalate_reason: A required pipeline property cannot be tested with the current design: status changes need a single gate (for example setStatus(doc, status, actor) with an authenticated actor and an audit record) before tests can attempt the owner's transition as each role and the coordinator and check it is refused and logged.
actions_now: Write no tests that would pretend to prove the property; escalate to the architect and the binding owner that the design needs a single, logged status gate, and state the tests (each role and the coordinator attempting approved, refused and logged) that will be written once it exists.

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether the remaining roles in the sequence still run for a unit after a failure, or whether other units continue; tests assert only the recorded failure and the absence of a substituted result.

covered: Throw records a failure
Timeout records a failure and does not substitute the cached result, with and without a cache

spec_findings: The spec does not state the order of units in the bundle or the JSON formatting (key order, indentation, trailing newline); determinism needs one fixed order, and the spec owner should name it.
The spec does not say what assemble does with an empty directory, a malformed unit file or non-unit files in the directory.
covered: Byte-identical output across repeated runs, file order, mtimes and clock, time zone, locale and absolute path; sensitivity to a changed input
not_covered: True cross-machine runs (different OS or Node versions) are approximated by environment variation, not run on separate machines
Empty or malformed input directories, pending the spec owner

tests.name: a ticket labelled urgent is routed to the on-call queue
tests.rule: A ticket labelled urgent is routed to the on-call queue
tests.setup: Replace classify with a stub behind the same interface (module mock of src/llm/client.js) returning 'urgent'
tests.expected: The ticket is in the on-call queue

tests.name: a ticket with any other label is not routed to on-call
tests.rule: Only urgent goes to the on-call queue
tests.setup: Stub classify returning each non-urgent label in turn
tests.expected: None is in the on-call queue

tests.name: routing uses the label, not the ticket text
tests.rule: Routing follows the label
tests.setup: Stub returns 'urgent' for a calm text and 'low' for a text full of 'URGENT'
tests.expected: Only the first goes to on-call

spec_findings: The spec does not say where a ticket goes when classify throws, times out or returns an unknown label, or whether label matching is case-sensitive.
defects: The existing tests call the real model API with a key from the environment, so they depend on the network, a secret and a non-deterministic model; they should be replaced by stubs or recorded responses.
covered: Routing of urgent and non-urgent labels with a stubbed classifier
not_covered: Whether the model labels tickets correctly; that is an evaluation of model behavior, for agent-evals
Classifier errors and unknown labels, pending the spec owner
actions_now: Write the routing tests with classify stubbed behind its interface, report that the existing live-API tests are non-deterministic, and route model labelling accuracy to agent-evals.

tests.name: draft output of a unit built on dq-7 carries the provisional flag
tests.rule: Provisional stays provisional: draft step
tests.setup: Decision dq-7 recorded as provisional; a unit built on dq-7
tests.expected: The output's flags field contains provisional with a reference to dq-7

tests.name: check output keeps the provisional flag even when the check passes
tests.rule: Provisional stays provisional: check step
tests.setup: Draft output carrying the dq-7 provisional flag; the check passes
tests.expected: The output's flags still contain provisional dq-7, alongside any flags the check adds

tests.name: bundle output keeps the provisional flag on the unit
tests.rule: Provisional stays provisional: bundle step
tests.setup: Checked output carrying the dq-7 flag, bundled with units not built on dq-7
tests.expected: The dq-7 unit carries provisional dq-7 in the bundle; the flag is not dropped or merged away

tests.name: a step that writes its own flags does not overwrite the inherited ones
tests.rule: The flag is carried through every step
tests.setup: Input with flags [provisional dq-7]; a step that sets a flag of its own (for example a check warning)
tests.expected: Output flags contain both the step's flag and provisional dq-7

tests.name: a unit not built on a provisional decision carries no provisional flag
tests.rule: The flag marks only units downstream of a provisional decision
tests.setup: A unit built only on confirmed decisions
tests.expected: No provisional flag at any step

tests.name: a unit built on another dq-7 unit inherits the flag
tests.rule: Every unit downstream of a provisional decision carries the flag
tests.setup: Unit U2 built on unit U1, which is built on dq-7
tests.action: Run the three steps on U2
tests.expected: U2 carries provisional dq-7 at every step

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether a bundle containing any provisional unit is itself flagged provisional at the bundle level.
The spec does not say what happens to the flag when dq-7 is later confirmed or reversed (cleared, rebuilt, or kept with history).
covered: The flag through draft, check and bundle, preserved when a step adds its own flags, inherited by dependent units, absent for units without provisional dependencies
not_covered: Bundle-level flagging and the flag's fate on confirmation or reversal of dq-7, pending the spec owner
actions_now: Write tests that follow a dq-7 unit through draft, check and bundle and assert the flag at each step, plus the negative and inherited cases, and send the bundle-level and confirmation questions to the spec owner.
